counterexample.note: The start moves to startTick + 1 only when the end tick is not aligned and the start tick's liquidityNet is not zero. Here the end tick 50 is aligned, so tick 100 is skipped even though its liquidityNet is +L. The walk ends at L instead of 0.

summary: Sets currentTick to startTick + 1 only when the start tick is aligned, the end tick is not aligned, and the start tick's liquidityNet is not zero. With an aligned end tick, or an initialized start tick whose liquidityNet is zero, the start tick is still skipped.
